data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The single expert is more reliable because 'objectively verifiable outcomes' in complex domains often depend on 'latent variables' that checklists cannot capture, making the panel's reliability a fragile artifact of the checklist's specific scope.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task is 'additive' (the outcome is the sum of independent binary checks).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The expert is suffering from 'overfitting' (applying a pattern that no longer fits the current case).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist was authored by a 'super-expert' who successfully captured all latent variables.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The expert's intuition is a compressed representation of high-dimensional data. In tasks where the 'verifiable outcome' depends on the interaction of variables (rather than a sum of parts), the checklist will systematically miss the 'interaction effect'. The expert's reliability is higher because their mechanism\u2014subconscious pattern matching\u2014operates on the full dimensionality of the problem, whereas the panel is constrained by the checklist's limited dimensionality.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
